selected_mbs_title: Summary of Doter Guvali Manganese Ore Block
exploration_agency_source: Geological Survey of India.
borehole_summary_source: 1 scout borehole (SBH-3) with 80.0 m meterage.
geological_resources_source: NA; the selected MBS does not estimate a block resource.
grade_source: Trench and grab samples reach 34.9% Mn; four drilled intervals are reported at 3.66%, 1.254%, 0.716% and 1.09% Mn.
mineral_zones_source: Two manganese ore bands were traced during large scale mapping in Rampura and Doter area. The largest exposed manganese band in in Rampura and Doter area have a strike length of 110 m and width between 6 - 10 m. Pinch and swell structures are seen in some of the outcrops in this area. The main ore body is trending 325° N. The manganese bands are lensoidal and elongated in nature due to deformation and remobilization. The manganese ore in this area is of low grade hosted within carbonate- phyllite and to some extent in brecciated quartzite. In one scout drilling in the block area intersected four different mineralized zones in SBH-3 drilled in Anas River block. Weighted average grades at different intervals of SBH-3 are; 3.66%, 1.254%, 0.716%, and 1.09% for intervals 1.0m to 2.5m (i.e. 1.5m), 23.9m to 29.8m (i.e. 5.9m), 33.0m to 38.0m (i.e. 5.0m), and 40.4m to 49.4m (i.e. 9.0m), respectively. For Scout borehole - 3(SBH-3), the minimum and maximum values for Mn percentage have been found to be 0.66 % (SBH3CS8) and 7.16% (SBH3CS1). The depth persistence of these ores is low due to the structural confinement of ore in the closures of folds, which are up to shallow levels. NATURE OF MINERALIZATION Main ore minerals of manganese are braunite and pyrolusite. Rhodochrosite has also been found in the hydrothermal veins near the ore bodies. The nature of origin of manganese ore is syngenetic. The primary deposition of manganese ore was followed by tight to isoclinal folding resulting in boudinaging of brittle manganese ore bearing horizon in the phyllitic country rock. After boudinaging the localization of manganese ore in the hinges of mesoscopic F2 folds might have taken place.
dip_strike_source: NNW-SSE strike and dips between 50° - 85° towards west.
thickness_source: Two manganese bands were traced during the large-scale mapping. The largest exposed manganese band in in Rampura and Doter area have a strike length of around 100m and width around 4m each. JUSTIFICATION FOR FURTHER EXPLORATION Manganese band in the proposed Doter-Guvali Block (7.35 Sq km; 735 Hectares) exposed in Rampura and Doter area have a strike length of around 100m and width around 4m each. The manganese bands are lensoidal and elongated in nature due to deformation and remobilization and one scout boreholes have been drilled and chemical analyses of core samples of SBH-3 revealed the minimum percentage of manganese is 0.66% and maximum is 7.16% Mn. Therefore, the presence of Manganese mineralization in the proposed Doter-Guvali manganese Block is recommended for further next stage of detailed exploration to know the continuity of mineralization, depth persistence and assessment of the resource. hydrography_source: Local Surface Drainage Pattern (Channels) During monsoon the rainwater runoff from the mine working area and waste dump are diverted to the mine pits through trenches and garland drains where primary settling of sediment take place. Pumped out water will be diverted into settling ponds and filter beds, where lime & flocculants is added to expedite the sediment settling rate and only clear water is allowed to flow out of mining lease area. Trenches are cleared before the onset of monsoon every year, so that all the water from dumps and mine working faces is diverted to a settling pond. Rivers/ Streams Towards north of the lease, a Nalla flows from east to northwest ultimately joining the main river downstream. There is a perennial river (Cudnem River) is running along the northern boundary of the lease which is one of the tributaries to Madei River. 8
